fieldNotes.siteResolution: Confirmed via web search (LoopNet APN 0238-133-12, Rexford Industrial property page, Waze 'Arrowhead Bottling Plant') as the Primo Brands / BlueTriton (formerly Nestle Waters / Arrowhead) bottling plant at 5772 E Jurupa St, Ontario CA 91761 - a 360,000 sqft single-tenant industrial building. Supplied coords (34.0365,-117.5931) landed in the public road / west parking frontage; the building center is ~34.03635,-117.59140, one block east. Jurupa St forms the north boundary; the lot is nearly north-aligned with only a slight rotation, so the geofences are kept as tight rectangles per the confirm-or-improve rule.
fieldNotes.truckGate: TRUE (medium confidence). The truck/dock yard occupies the EAST side of the building and is fully enclosed by a continuous ~8ft tilt-up concrete SCREEN WALL that runs the entire Jurupa St frontage and wraps the NE corner onto the east internal street (confirmed in Street View sv11/sv12/sv13 2025-02 and sv07/sv08, and in z21 satellite p21). A walled, screened yard with a single controlled vehicle break on the east internal street = a gated truck entrance. I could NOT capture the actual gate panel head-on: the east internal street (~ -117.5903) has no Street View pano (coverage snaps one block east to the next building's back wall) and the break is screened by pine trees. Marked true on the walled-yard configuration but flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.guardShack: FALSE (medium-high confidence). No booth-sized structure (1-3 vehicle footprint, multi-side windows) appears at ANY entrance across all satellite (z20-21) and Street View frames. The west office/employee entry from the west cross street is fully OPEN and ungated (sv09 SW corner shows an open driveway with only a stop sign and hydrant). The east yard is walled with no visible guard booth at the wall break.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: TRUE - a truck gate is present (walled yard) but there is no guard shack, implying kiosk / call-box / app or office-buzzer check-in. Inherits the truckGate uncertainty.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 0-10 band. The bottling plant ships palletized water through a MODEST dock operation on the EAST face, north portion, under a dock canopy/awning (gray strip in p12/p14 z20) with 2 trailers backed in. No long continuous dock-door rhythm is visible on any face (N, S and W faces are blank tilt-up walls per p11, sv02). Estimated ~8-10 doors under the east canopy; banded 0-10. NOTE: the separate gray cross-dock building immediately SOUTH (across a shared drive aisle) has a large dock bank but is a DIFFERENT facility and is excluded.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 0-10 band. The east yard is mostly employee parking (rows of cars, consistent with 500-1000 employees per Cortera/BlueTriton hiring posts) plus stacked lumber/pallets and a couple of trailers (one bobtail/white trailer + canopy trailers). Only a handful of drop trailers without tractors are visible; banded 0-10. Not a dedicated drop-trailer storage lot, so dropYard=false.
fieldNotes.dropYard: FALSE - no dedicated trailer-storage lot; the east area is dominated by employee parking with only incidental trailer/pallet staging.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: TRUE (low-medium) - the open paved east yard inside the wall, between the dock canopy and the parking, can hold trucks queuing for the docks.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The east yard is deep (building-to-east-street ~80-100m of paved yard) and can hold 3+ trucks queued before the dock canopy; drivewayLong=true.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: Single walled yard with one controlled break on the east internal street = trucks enter and exit at the same point; entryExitTogether=true, lanes ~1 in / 1 out (not directly observable, low confidence).
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: FALSE - a single dock cluster on the east face; no second physically separate dock bank on the Primo building.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Urban - the site sits inside the dense Ontario / Inland Empire-West industrial fabric (Ontario Airport logistics corridor), surrounded on all sides by large distribution buildings.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: FALSE - dense metro/industrial area, strong cellular coverage expected.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: FALSE - the truck yard is set well back from Jurupa St behind a deep buffer and the deep east yard provides ample internal stacking; a queue would not spill onto the public road.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: FALSE - single modest gate break; no wide multi-lane apron or unused paved width that would obviously support an express bypass.
fieldNotes.scale: FALSE - no truck scale / weigh pad visible in the truck path.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: FALSE - one Primo building on the fenced parcel; the adjacent buildings (west, south gray cross-dock, east) are separate tenants/parcels.
fieldNotes.railServed: FALSE - no rail spur enters the property; access is road-only.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: 1 - the single 360,000 sqft Primo/Arrowhead bottling building. Minor utility/electrical cabinets in the yard not counted.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~11 acres for the fenced Primo parcel (employee parking W + building + walled east yard), derived from the perimeter rectangle (~270m E-W x ~170m N-S). The 360k sqft building footprint dominates; exact building outline is approximate from overhead imagery.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~2 under the east dock canopy + ~2 bobtail/box trailers in the yard = ~4. Most vehicles on site are employee cars, not trailers.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: The open east yard could practically hold ~15 trailers if cleared of pallet staging; honest overhead estimate.
fieldNotes.imageryQuality: Good high-resolution Maxar/Airbus satellite (z20-21 usable) and 2025-02 + 2023-12 Street View on Jurupa St and the west cross street. The single blind spot is the east internal street truck gate (no pano coverage + tree screening), which is the sole reason truckGate/remoteGs are medium not high.
